title: Levels draws its live L1 and L2 on the camera's stage, against formula rule 1
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx renders the arriving level and the L2 overlay inside `.dk-stage`, the element the camera transforms, so at L1 the records are scaled x3 and translated out of the clipped scene, and at L2 the overlay is scaled x7 and clipped.

## Description
Levels.tsx:184 wraps every live layer (the L0 list, the L1 list at :207, the overlay at :236) in `<div className="dk-stage">`, and the subscribe at :129 writes `poseToTransform(pose)` onto it. useSemanticZoom flies the camera to `poseFor` on every nav change (:147: zoom 3 at L1, 7 at L2, pan y -72 x group index). But the template SWAPS layers rather than drawing one world: the L1 list is a new, short list starting at y=0, so it is rendered under a pose computed for the L0 list. app/globals.css:68-71 clips `.dk-levels` (`overflow: clip`) and :83 gives the stage `will-change: transform`, which makes the stage the containing block of the overlay's `position: fixed` (globals.css `.dk-overlay`), so the overlay rides the camera and the clip. The echo (`.dk-echo`, globals.css:129-131, `inset: 0`) is sized to the arriving level's height and crops the outgoing level to a strip; atlas found and fixed exactly this (examples/atlas/KIT-GAPS.md #12, `.at-echo { height: 100dvh }`) and the template never took the fix. The section also changes height from ~1282px (23 rows) to ~50px at L1, so the records table below jumps by about 1230px on every level change. docs/layered-ui-formula.md §1 rule 1: "Only the leaving level may hold a transform ... let the live layer mount at its final size"; rule 11: one owner per element's transform; rule 10: rules 1-3 are for layouts that swap, a camera is for one continuous space. The file's header asserts the opposite of what it does (Levels.tsx:16 "The live layer mounts at its final size") and cites "the nine rules" of §1, which has eighteen. Fixed looks like one of two designs, which is why this is a direction call: (a) a continuous sheet, every level drawn in one world and the camera moving over it, poseFor/resolve* inverses by construction (rule 16, the atlas pattern); or (b) a swapping skeleton with no camera on the live layers, the echo alone carrying the move (rule 1), and the overlay outside the stage.

## Flow
- Open the template's list page; click any owner but the first (nav.openGroup)
- useSemanticZoom flies the rig to poseFor: translate(0, -216k px) scale(3) on .dk-stage, which now holds a one-record list of height ~50px
- The visible band of the stage is [h/3 + 72k, 2h/3 + 72k] in list coordinates: for h=50 and k>=1 it lies wholly below the content, so the scene is blank; for k=0 it is the middle third of one row, magnified x3
- Click a record: the overlay mounts inside the stage at zoom 7, positioned against the stage, and is clipped by .dk-levels

## Expected impact
Every app copied from the template starts from a three-depth read whose second and third depths do not render; the person copying it meets this before writing any domain code. Measured by: L1 rows fully visible per owner (0 of 23 today) and overlay scale at L2 (7 today, 1 expected). Could break: the echo/morph timing, which only a browser shows.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - L1 and L2 are visible, at scale 1, after a level change
Before: probe: with the kit's poseToTransform and the template's poses (STEP 72, ZOOM [1,3,7]) and the stylesheet's row (12+12 padding, 24px line, 2px border, 6px gap = 56px pitch), a full L1 row is visible for 0 of 23 owners (owner 0 shows a x3 middle-third strip); the L2 overlay is drawn at scale 7 inside a clipped box
After: design (b) by construction: L1 and the overlay have no camera ancestor, scale 1; design (a) by the atlas precedent (lanes.poses.test.ts asserts poseFor/resolve inverses per node)
Method: probe - arithmetic on the kit's pure poseToTransform and the template's constants; the rendered result needs a browser, and the choice between (a) and (b) is a design call
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:16  * ... The live layer mounts at its final size
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:7  ... the nine rules in `docs/layered-ui-formula.md` §1 (docs/layered-ui-formula.md §1 lists 18)
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:147  poseFor: (to) => ({ zoom: ZOOM[to.level], pan: { x: 0, y: -STEP * indexOf(to.group) } })
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:184  <div className="dk-stage" ref={stageRef}>   (L0 list, L1 list :207 and <Overlay> :236 all inside)
examples/demo-kit/template/app/globals.css:71  overflow: clip;   (.dk-levels)
examples/demo-kit/template/app/globals.css:83  will-change: transform;   (.dk-stage: containing block for the fixed overlay)
examples/demo-kit/template/app/globals.css:131  inset: 0;   (.dk-echo, cropped to the arriving level)
examples/atlas/KIT-GAPS.md:752-757  the template's .dk-echo `inset: 0` "cropped it to a strip; it needs one screenful"
docs/layered-ui-formula.md:39-43 rule 1: "Only the leaving level may hold a transform"
impact: Every app copied from the template starts from a three-depth read whose second and third depths do not render; the person copying it meets this before writing any domain code. Measured by: L1 rows fully visible per owner (0 of 23 today) and overlay scale at L2 (7 today, 1 expected). Could break: the echo/morph timing, which only a browser shows.

title: The camera scene is a page-tall list, so it eats wheel and touch scroll
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:181 spreads the rig's bind over an in-flow list about 1282px tall, so a wheel over it is preventDefault'ed and zooms (and past band 2 opens an owner), and `touch-action: none` stops touch scrolling over most of a phone screen.

## Description
useCameraRig attaches a non-passive wheel listener that always calls `event.preventDefault()` (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useCameraRig.ts:509) and puts `style: { touchAction: "none" }` in `bind` (:121); Levels.tsx:121-122 asks for `drag: "pan"` and `wheel: "zoom"`. That is right for a bounded canvas (atlas's `.al-canvas` is one), but the template's scene is the `.dk-levels` section in the page flow, one row per owner: 23 rows, about 1282px, above the records table (app/page.tsx:15-16). A reader scrolling the page down to the table with the pointer over the owners zooms the camera instead; a long enough scroll crosses band 2 and useSemanticZoom opens whatever group it resolves (see the card on the wrong owner). On touch, the section takes the pan, so the page cannot be scrolled while the finger is over it. Fixed looks like: either a bounded scene (a fixed block-size, the level scrolling inside it, as atlas does) or `wheel: "none"`/a modifier-gated wheel and `drag: "none"` on a list that is not a canvas. Which one depends on the direction chosen for the Levels card, hence C.

## Flow
- Open the template's list page at 1280x800; put the pointer over the owner list and scroll down to reach the records table
- The rig's wheel listener preventDefaults every tick and zooms; past zoom 2.16 (band 2 plus 8% hysteresis) useSemanticZoom dispatches nav.openGroup
- On a phone, a vertical swipe starting over the owner list pans the camera (touch-action: none) and the page does not scroll

## Expected impact
Anyone using a copy of the template with a mouse wheel or a phone; measured by whether a wheel or swipe over the Levels list scrolls the page (no today). Could break: semantic zoom by wheel, if the fix removes the wheel rather than bounding the scene.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the page scrolls when the reader scrolls it
Before: every wheel tick over a 1282px band of the page is consumed (preventDefault at useCameraRig.ts:509); touch-action none over the same band
After: predicted: a bounded scene leaves the page scroll outside it; wheel:none leaves it everywhere. Falsified if a browser shows the page scrolling over the list today
Method: simulation - read from the rig's listener and the template's layout; needs a browser (and a phone viewport) to take the figure
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useCameraRig.ts:509  event.preventDefault();   (native, passive: false)
examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useCameraRig.ts:121  style: { touchAction: "none" };
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:121-122  drag: "pan", wheel: "zoom"
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:181  {...rig.bind}   on <section className="dk-levels"> (in page flow)
examples/demo-kit/template/app/page.tsx:15-16  <Levels rows={rows} /> above <RecordsTable rows={rows} />
impact: Anyone using a copy of the template with a mouse wheel or a phone; measured by whether a wheel or swipe over the Levels list scrolls the page (no today). Could break: semantic zoom by wheel, if the fix removes the wheel rather than bounding the scene.

instrument: Move poseFor/resolveGroup out of Levels.tsx into a pure module that takes the drawn row pitch, and a test that runs the kit's zoomAt from REST_POSE with the pointer over each row k until the band is crossed and asserts resolveGroup returns k (today 1 of 23)
title: Wheel-zooming the owner list opens a different owner than the one pointed at
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:77 and :148 resolve the group under the camera with `STEP = 72` from the list's top, but the stylesheet draws a 56px pitch and the kit's zoomAt anchors about the frame's centre, so a wheel over row k opens the owner under the pointer for 1 of 23 rows.

## Description
resolveGroup is `groups[round(-pan.y / STEP)]` (Levels.tsx:148-149) and poseFor is its inverse (:147), so the pair is self-consistent (formula rule 14) but not consistent with the scene: STEP is commented as "the row height the stylesheet draws" (:76) while `.dk-level-row` is 12+12 padding, a 24px line and 2px of border, plus the `.dk-level` gap of 6px, i.e. 56px; and pan 0 means the frame's centre is centred (zoomAt solves pan about the middle of the box, examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/camera.ts zoomAt), while index 0 is the TOP row. A hand-kept number mirroring CSS, plus an origin mismatch. Fixed looks like: poses derived from the drawn geometry (measured, or a pitch token the CSS and the poses share), indexed about the frame centre, with a test. Moot if the Levels direction card drops the camera from this skeleton.

## Flow
- At L0 put the pointer over owner row 22 (the last) and wheel in
- zoomAt keeps that point fixed: pan.y = (y22 - H/2)(1/z - 1), about -308 scene units at z = 2.16
- resolveGroup = round(308/72) = 4 -> nav.openGroup(groups[4]); the reader pointed at owner 22 and is flown to owner 4

## Expected impact
Anyone wheeling into a group in a copy of the template; measured as the share of rows whose wheel opens that row (1/23 today). Could break: the band hysteresis, if the poses' scale changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the wheel opens the owner under the pointer
Before: probe (kit's zoomAt, template's STEP and band, 56px pitch, 23 owners): 1 of 23 rows open their own owner; rows 0-12 all open owner 0
After: with pitch 56 and centre-origin poses the same probe maps k -> k by construction (rule 14)
Method: probe - the kit's pure zoomAt in node over the template's constants; the drawn pitch is read off the stylesheet and needs a browser to confirm
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Anyone wheeling into a group in a copy of the template; measured as the share of rows whose wheel opens that row (1/23 today). Could break: the band hysteresis, if the poses' scale changes.

title: The template's Levels has no on-screen way back up from L1 or L2
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx draws no breadcrumb or back control, so at L1 a pointer-only reader without a wheel has no way back to L0 (Escape is keyboard-only; drag pans).

## Description
The kit leaves the way back to each app on purpose (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/index.ts:16: "the level rail, the breadcrumb and the back affordance are where a direction earns its identity, so each one draws its own"), and the template, the starting point for every direction, draws none: L1 (Levels.tsx:207-233) is a list of record buttons and nothing else. The ways up are Escape (the nav's window listener), a wheel-out past band 1, or the overlay's Close at L2, which returns to L1 only. A trackpad without scroll gestures, a touch screen (pinch works, but nothing says so) and a mouse without a wheel are stuck at L1 until reload. This is not the challenge run's URL-held-levels card (browser Back and reload restoring the level); it is the on-screen control. Fixed looks like: at focus.level > 0 a plain button ("All owners", or the owner's name as a crumb) calling nav.up, styled with the template's row class.

## Flow
- Open the list page, click an owner (L1)
- Look for a way back: there is no control; drag pans the camera; clicking empty space does nothing
- Only Escape, a wheel-out or reload returns to L0

## Expected impact
Every copy's first reader on a pointer without a wheel; measured as on-screen controls that leave L1 (0 today, 1 after). Could break: nothing; the button calls the same nav.up as Escape.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a reader can leave L1 with the pointer alone
Before: 0 on-screen controls call nav.up at L1
After: 1 (predicted); falsified if the kit already draws one into the template's tree
Method: simulation - read from the JSX; no DOM instrument in the kit's node tests and no browser in this round
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The seed gives almost every owner one record, so L1 is a one-row list
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/lib/db.ts:30 draws a fresh `rng.fullName()` per record, so the 24 records fall into 23 owners and Levels' middle depth (one owner's records) is a single row for 22 of them.

## Description
Levels groups by `owner` (Levels.tsx:107-111) to make L0 (owners) -> L1 (that owner's records) -> L2 (one record). The seed (db.ts:29-45) draws each record's owner independently from the name generator, so owners almost never repeat: the three-depth demo every copy starts from has an L1 that adds nothing over L0, and the L0 count beside every name reads 1. Fixed looks like: draw a small owner pool once (`Array.from({ length: 5 }, () => rng.fullName())`) and `rng.pick` from it per record. The seed stays deterministic; an existing copy keeps its database until `data/` is removed.

## Flow
- Fresh copy, first run: seed() inserts 24 records with 24 independent owner draws
- Levels L0 shows 23 owners, 22 with the count 1
- Opening any of those 22 shows a one-record L1

## Expected impact
The person copying the template judges the layered formula on this data; measured as groups with 2+ records (1 of 23 today). Could break: nothing outside the template; the activity seed row says 24 records either way.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the middle depth has something to compare
Before: probe (the kit's rngFor, the seed's draw order): 23 owners, sizes 1,2,1,1,... (one group of 2)
After: probe with a pool of 5 drawn first: 5 owners, sizes 2,5,7,6,4
Method: probe - the kit's seed copied to a scratch dir with its import made loadable and both arms run; not Lane A because no gate in the tree can load the seed yet
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The person copying the template judges the layered formula on this data; measured as groups with 2+ records (1 of 23 today). Could break: nothing outside the template; the activity seed row says 24 records either way.

title: Nothing typechecks the template; its README promises a script that never existed
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/README.md:11-17 tells the reader `scripts/check-template.mjs` typechecks the template after any kit change; no such script was ever in this repository, the workspace globs skip the template, and so no gate sees a kit change that breaks it.

## Description
The template is deliberately not a workspace package (pnpm-workspace.yaml matches `examples/*`; the template is one level deeper), and the kit's tsconfig includes only `src/**`. README.md:11-17 says the hole is closed by `scripts/check-template.mjs` - `git log --all -S check-template` finds the string only in the commits that wrote the README and examples/atlas/KIT-GAPS.md, never the file. So a change to the kit's exported types (as the sibling round on webmcp is making today to `useWebMCPTool`'s types) can break every future copy silently. The same README is stale elsewhere: README.md:23 lists the existing apps as `ledgerbox`, `hirelane`, `tidycrm`, `clonedeck` (no clonedeck; atlas is the fourth), and README.md:81 says Levels.tsx "is about a hundred lines" (322). Out of this round's paths: README.md and scripts/ are not in the context's file list. Fixed looks like: the script exists and runs in the root gate; the README's app list names a role instead of apps (as this round did for the template's code comments in 34ccc7b) and drops the line count.

## Flow
- Change an exported type in examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp (e.g. a required field on useWebMCPTool's options)
- pnpm typecheck: green (the template is in no package's include)
- A copy made afterwards fails `pnpm --filter <app> typecheck` at the README's own step

## Expected impact
Every future copy; measured as gates that typecheck the template (0 today). Could break: the root gate's duration (one extra tsc over 17 files, about 5s here).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a kit change that breaks the template fails a gate
Before: 0 gates reach the template; `node scripts/check-template.mjs` fails with module not found
After: out-of-tree check built this round: template tsc exit 0, eslint exit 0, a seeded type error exits 2
Method: probe - the instrument was built in the scratchpad and run on the real template; not landed because scripts/ and the root package.json are outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

instrument: A parity test in examples/demo-kit/test: every dependency the template's package.json shares with the workspace apps (examples/*/package.json with an app/layout.tsx) pins the same version; red today on @types/react and @types/react-dom
title: The template pins @types/react 19.2.18, which a3fecd5 removed from every app
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/package.json:25-26 pins @types/react 19.2.18 and @types/react-dom 19.2.7, while a3fecd5 moved the kit and all four apps to 19.3.0 because two copies made "every intrinsic element ... an error"; a copy reinstalls the second copy.

## Description
a3fecd5 (chore(examples): one React types version) explains the failure: with two @types/react in the tree the JSX augmentation lands on the wrong module. It changed examples/demo-kit, hirelane, ledgerbox and tidycrm (atlas came later at 19.3.0) but not the template's package.json. node_modules/.pnpm holds only @types+react@19.3.0 today, so a copy's `pnpm install` brings 19.2.18 back. The template typechecks out of tree only because that check borrowed an app's 19.3.0. Out of this round's paths: template/package.json is not in the context's file list (nor in any other context). Fixed looks like: 19.3.0 / 19.3.0, with the parity test so the next bump cannot miss it.

## Flow
- cp -r examples/demo-kit/template examples/newapp; pnpm install
- pnpm resolves @types/react 19.2.18 for newapp and 19.3.0 for the kit it imports
- pnpm --filter newapp typecheck meets the duplicate-types failure a3fecd5 describes

## Expected impact
Every copy at the README's first gate; measured as distinct @types/react versions after a copy's install (2 predicted, 1 after). Could break: nothing; it is the version every app already runs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a copy installs one React types version
Before: template pins 19.2.18 / 19.2.7; kit and the four apps pin 19.3.0 / 19.3.0
After: the same versions everywhere (by inspection)
Method: probe - the version pairs read across the five package.json files and the store; the duplicate-types failure itself is a3fecd5's measurement, not re-run (it needs an install)
Result: better
Gate: none

examples/{atlas,hirelane,ledgerbox,tidycrm}/package.json and examples/demo-kit/package.json: "@types/react": "19.3.0", "@types/react-dom": "19.3.0"
git show a3fecd5: "the JSX augmentation landed on the wrong module and every intrinsic element became an error"
$ ls node_modules/.pnpm | grep ^@types+react@   -> @types+react@19.3.0 only
impact: Every copy at the README's first gate; measured as distinct @types/react versions after a copy's install (2 predicted, 1 after). Could break: nothing; it is the version every app already runs.

instrument: A browser trace (or motion's onAnimationStart/Complete timestamps logged in a dev build) showing the overlay's ink starts after the box lands on open and finishes before the box leaves on close
title: The L2 overlay fades its text in while its box is still flying, against rule 3
body:
## Summary
examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:314 starts the overlay's ink fade at mount, concurrently with the box's layout morph, and on close the ink unmounts with the box; formula rule 3 is "Box, then ink ... both directions".

## Description
docs/layered-ui-formula.md:47-48 rule 3: containers move first, text arrives after the box has landed and leaves before the box travels back. The Overlay's box takes `transition={layout}` (the `move` token, 260ms) and its content `initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} transition={transition}` (the `fade` token, 160ms, no delay), so the text is fully in at 160ms while the box is still morphing; closing removes both at once (the Overlay is deliberately outside AnimatePresence for rule 2). The header lists rules 1, 2, 4-8 and skips 3. Fixed looks like: the ink's transition delayed by the move duration on open (both read from the tokens already in scope), and on close the ink faded out before nav.up commits, or the header saying the template does not implement rule 3.

## Flow
- Click a record at L1: the card morphs into the overlay over 260ms
- The title and note fade in over 0-160ms, i.e. while the box is mid-flight
- Close: text and box vanish together; the box morphs home with no ink-first exit

## Expected impact
Visual polish of every copy's L2 open/close; measured as ink start minus box end (about -100ms today, >= 0 after). Could break: perceived latency of the open, by up to one move duration.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - text arrives after its box, as rule 3 says
Before: ink fade 0-160ms, box morph 0-260ms (from the tokens): ink done 100ms before the box lands
After: ink 260-420ms on open (predicted from the same tokens)
Method: simulation - token arithmetic over the JSX; the timing needs a browser
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:

examples/demo-kit/template/components/Levels.tsx:314  <motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} transition={transition}>
examples/demo-kit/template/app/globals.css  --dk-dur-move: 260ms; --dk-dur-fade: 160ms
